home.intro: Follow the biblical record across the ancient world — patriarchs, Old Testament battles, the birth and ministry of Jesus, and the apostles. Every place, date and claim is cited, and contested points are shown as such.

sourcing.title: How we source
sourcing.body: Dates are shown as ranges, not false single-year precision. Genesis 1–11 is dated from Scripture’s own genealogies (Genesis 5 and 11): on the Masoretic numbers Ussher used, Creation is 4004 BC and the Earth is about six thousand years old; archaeology dates the human layers in that story — flood silt, cities, royal waterworks — not the forming of the planet, and those finds are drawn as complementary setting, not as a second clock. Each claim carries citations, a confidence level, and a review status. Claims in this build are not specialist-signed — this project checked them, and a qualified historical geographer has not yet signed them off, so a store release is blocked until that happens. Tertiary sources — Wikipedia, popular encyclopedias, study-Bible maps, devotional sites — are only ever orienting links, never the sole authority: every claim is also backed by a concrete source (a primary text, a standard scholarly work, an excavation report, or a gazetteer), and the content build blocks any claim that rests on tertiary sources alone. High-confidence coordinates must additionally carry a place-specific citation or a Pleiades gazetteer id — a whole-atlas reference is not enough. Ambiguous locations draw every rival candidate as a hollow marker and list them in the site panel, rather than implying a single pin. Route strokes are drawn by geometry grade so a surveyed Roman road never looks like a schematic connector. Where scholars or traditions disagree, we say so. Bible text is public domain (King James Version, American Standard Version). This atlas is carefully cited and reviewed — it does not claim to be definitive.
